facts.fact_text: Following the February-March 2003 presidential election in Armenia, the applicant participated in a series of rallies of protest organised in Yerevan by the opposition parties.
On 7 April 2003 at 5 p.m. a demonstration was held in the centre of Yerevan on the occasion of Mother's Day.
The demonstration of 7 April 2003 appears to have been of a political nature.
During the demonstration of 7 April 2003, criticism of the Government and of the conduct of the presidential election was voiced.
The applicant took part in the demonstration of 7 April 2003.
The applicant took part in the march that followed the demonstration of 7 April 2003.
At the Central District Police Station of Yerevan, the applicant found out that she had been arrested for having participated in the demonstration of 7 April 2003.
At the Central District Police Station of Yerevan, the arresting police officers drew up a record of the applicant's arrest (արձանագրություն բերման ենթարկելու մասին).

One of the arresting police officers reported to the Head of the Central District Police Station of Yerevan (ՀՀ ոստիկանության Երևան քաղաքի կենտրոնական բաժնի պետ) that the applicant was brought to the Central District Police Station for having participated on 7 April 2003 in an unauthorised march headed from the Research Institute of Ancient Manuscripts (Մատենադարան) to the Constitutional Court and violated public order.

On 7 April 2003 at around 12 midnight the applicant was taken to Judge M. of the Kentron and Nork-Marash District Court of Yerevan (Երևան քաղաքի Կենտրոն և Նորք-Մարաշ համայնքների առաջին ատյանի դատարան), who examined the case.

Judge M. of the Kentron and Nork-Marash District Court of Yerevan, after a brief hearing, sentenced the applicant under Article 172 of the Code of Administrative Offences (CAO) to an administrative fine of 1500 Armenian drams (approximately EUR 2.4 at the material time) in relation to the events of 7 April 2003.
At 11 p.m. on 9 April 2003 the applicant was taken to Judge M. of the Kentron and Nork-Marash District Court of Yerevan, who examined the case.

Judge M. of the Kentron and Nork-Marash District Court of Yerevan sentenced the applicant under Article 172 of the Code of Administrative Offences (CAO) to five days of administrative detention in relation to the events of 9 April 2003.
According to the applicant, on her way home on 7 April 2003 she was approached by three men in civilian clothes who, without presenting themselves, started dragging her to a nearby car.
According to the applicant, the three men who approached her on 7 April 2003 twisted her arms, punched her and pushed her into the car.
According to the applicant, she screamed and tried to resist when the three men in civilian clothes attempted to drag her to a nearby car on 7 April 2003.
The applicant's actions on 7 April 2003 were qualified under Article 172 of the Code of Administrative Offences (Վարչական իրավախախտումների վերաբերյալ ՀՀ օրենսգիրք – "the CAO") as minor hooliganism.
The applicant's actions on 9 April 2003 were qualified under Article 172 of the Code of Administrative Offences (CAO) as minor hooliganism.

One of the arresting police officers reported to the Head of the Central District Police Station of Yerevan (ՀՀ ոստիկանության Երևան քաղաքի կենտրոնական բաժնի պետ) that the applicant was brought to the Central District Police Station for having participated on 7 April 2003 in an unauthorised march headed from the Research Institute of Ancient Manuscripts (Մատենադարան) to the Constitutional Court and violated public order.

The arresting police officers drew up a record of the applicant's arrest on 9 April 2003 in which it was stated that she had been "arrested for having violated public order during the march of 9 April 2003".

One of the arresting police officers reported to the Head of the Central District Police Station of Yerevan that during the march of 9 April 2003 after the demonstration next to the Research Institute of Ancient Manuscripts (Մատենադարան) he noticed one citizen who was violating public order: waving a flag while walking on the driveway, obstructing the regular traffic of public transport, creating an emergency situation, randomly hitting passers-by who were not taking part in the demonstration with the long flagpole, and inciting others to follow her example.
The applicant alleged that she was forced to sign the record of an administrative offence and other documents prepared by the police officers on 7 April 2003 under threat of violence.
The applicant alleged that the police officers persuaded her to refuse a lawyer on 7 April 2003 by insisting that a lawyer's involvement would not help and would only be detrimental to her case.
The Government contested the applicant's allegation that she was forced to sign documents under threat of violence on 7 April 2003.
According to the Government, the police officers explained to the applicant her right to have a lawyer on 7 April 2003 and advised her to avail herself of this right, which she did not wish to do.
According to the Government, the record of an administrative offence of 7 April 2003 was signed by the applicant voluntarily and without any objections.

According to the Government, the applicant failed to initiate any actions aimed at the defence of her rights on 7 April 2003, such as lodging motions or availing herself of other procedural rights guaranteed by Article 267 of the Code of Administrative Offences (CAO), despite having been made aware of them.

The applicant alleged, and the Government did not explicitly dispute, that the record of the court hearing of 7 April 2003 was a fake and was drafted at some point after the hearing in order to create an appearance of lawfulness.
The applicant alleged that in reality there was no clerk present at the court hearing of 7 April 2003 and the hearing was not being recorded.
The applicant alleged that the court hearing of 7 April 2003 lasted not more than five minutes and was conducted in Judge M.'s office.
The applicant alleged that, contrary to what the record stated, only Judge M., the applicant and the accompanying police officer were present at the court hearing of 7 April 2003.

The applicant alleged that the accompanying police officer at the court hearing of 7 April 2003 did not participate in the hearing and his functions were limited only to bringing the applicant before the judge.
The applicant alleged that at the court hearing of 7 April 2003, Judge M. neither explained her rights nor asked whether she wanted to have a lawyer.
The applicant alleged that at the court hearing of 7 April 2003, the materials of the case file were not read out and she was not allowed to make any oral submissions.
The applicant alleged that at the court hearing of 7 April 2003, no evidence was taken or examined.
The applicant alleged that at the court hearing of 7 April 2003, Judge M. prepared the decision solely on the basis of the materials prepared by the police.
The applicant alleged that at the court hearing of 7 April 2003, Judge M. threatened the applicant with imminent detention if she did not refrain from further participation in demonstrations.

Judge M. of the Kentron and Nork-Marash District Court of Yerevan sentenced the applicant under Article 172 of the Code of Administrative Offences (CAO) to five days of administrative detention in relation to the events of 9 April 2003.
According to the applicant, on her way home on 7 April 2003 she was approached by three men in civilian clothes who, without presenting themselves, started dragging her to a nearby car.
According to the applicant, the three men who approached her on 7 April 2003 twisted her arms, punched her and pushed her into the car.
According to the applicant, she screamed and tried to resist when the three men in civilian clothes attempted to drag her to a nearby car on 7 April 2003.
The applicant alleged that in reply to her complaint of 8 April 2003 she was asked to appear in two days.
It appears that the applicant did not pursue her complaint of 8 April 2003 to the Kentron and Nork-Marash District Prosecutor any further.
